# Requirements Document: Credentials and their data elements

## Introduction

The One ID guide stores both of its credentials, the photoid and the boarding
pass, in the ISO mdoc format (§4.1).  This module holds what the guide says
every such credential has: a document type, namespaces, data elements
identified within a namespace, and an end of validity.  The guide leaves the
rest of the format to ISO/IEC 18013-5, which this project has not read.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneId/Mdoc.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-id/blob/main/Rules/OneId/Mdoc.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet. *Sources* lists the sections of the guide each rule was written from, *External specifications* lists the specifications it relies on and whether this project has read each, and *Confirmation* says whether anyone outside the model has confirmed the rule as written.

## Requirements

### Requirement OID-106

**User Story:** As a relying party, I want to name one data element of a credential by its namespace and its identifier, so that I can request only that element and the wallet can disclose it without the others.

**Rule:** THE SYSTEM SHALL identify each data element of a credential by the name of its namespace and its identifier. (Lean: `Mdoc.element?`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1 Credential format and data model](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.1 photoid](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard)

**External specifications:** ISO/IEC 18013-5:2021, §6.3.1, §8.3.1, §8.3.2 (not read)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the namespace names of a credential and the identifiers within each namespace are unique THE SYSTEM SHALL return the value of each data element for the name of its namespace and its identifier.
   - OID-106.1, proven: proven theorem `element_addressable`
2. IF a credential has no data element with a given namespace name and identifier THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return no value for them.
   - OID-106.2, proven: proven theorem `element_absent`
3. IF two namespaces of a credential have the same name, or two data elements of one namespace have the same identifier THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the credential.
   - OID-106.3, open: open theorem `boardingPass_names_unique`; open theorem `photoid_names_unique`; counterexample `repeatedIdentifier`; counterexample `twoBoardingPassStrings`

#### Open question on OID-106.3

> The names in an accepted photoid are unique.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide leaves the structure of an mdoc to
> ISO/IEC 18013-5 and does not say that namespace names and data element
> identifiers are unique.  If they may repeat, a request for a name is
> ambiguous: the example `repeatedIdentifier` shows a photoid with two
> family names, of which a relying party receives one.  Is a credential in
> which a name repeats rejected?

#### Open question on OID-106.3

> The names in an accepted boarding pass are unique.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide does not say that namespace names
> and data element identifiers are unique.  If they may repeat, a boarding pass
> with two boarding pass strings is accepted, and a relying party receives one
> of them.  The example `twoBoardingPassStrings` shows it.  Is a credential
> in which a name repeats rejected?
